title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 12th District
area: Mostly the city of Charlotte and surrounding parts of Mecklenburg County.

context.text: Incumbent Alma Adams defeated one Democratic primary challenger with 78.9% of the vote. Jack Codiga won the Republican primary with 67.4% of the vote over one challenger.

summary.text: Alma Adams is the Democratic incumbent for North Carolina's 12th Congressional District. A former Bennett College art professor, she served on the Greensboro school board and city council and in the North Carolina House before winning a November 2014 special election to Congress. She serves on the House Agriculture and Education and Workforce Committees; her official biography highlights work on HBCU funding and Black maternal health.

background.text: Born in High Point, North Carolina, and attended high school in Newark, New Jersey, according to WFAE's 2026 voter guide.

According to her official biography, she graduated from North Carolina A&T State University in 1968, received a master's degree in art education in 1972, and earned a Ph.D. in art education and multicultural education from The Ohio State University in 1981.
Taught art at Bennett College for 40 years, according to her official biography, and led student voter-participation efforts there.

Began her political career in the 1980s as the first African American woman elected to the Greensboro school board, then served nine years on the Greensboro City Council before moving to the state legislature.

Appointed to North Carolina House District 26 in 1994 and served ten terms, including as chair of the North Carolina Legislative Black Caucus; her official biography credits her with the Displaced Homemakers Bill and the state's first minimum wage increase in nine years.
Won the November 2014 special election for the 12th District and was sworn in immediately as the 100th woman elected to the 113th Congress; she was elected to her sixth full term on November 5, 2024.

Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (Conservation, Research, and Biotechnology; Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture) and the Committee on Education and the Workforce for the 2025-2026 Congress; previously served on the Committee on Financial Services (2019-2022).

Her official biography lists the enactment of H.R. 5363, the FUTURE Act (permanent funding for Minority-Serving Institutions), among her legislative accomplishments; she founded and co-chairs the Congressional Bipartisan HBCU Caucus and co-founded and co-chairs the Black Maternal Health Caucus, which introduced the Momnibus package.
Has received the North Carolina A&T State University Human Rights Medal and was inducted into the National Black College Alumni Hall of Fame, according to her official biography.

priorities.text: As a retired educator, I have seen first-hand the impact a great education can have on a young person's life. I will always be a champion for public schools, our teachers, our children, and our HBCUs.
Health care is important to our district and to Congresswoman Adams' work in Congress; she has been a staunch and ardent supporter of the Affordable Care Act.
Congresswoman Adams is pushing for strong and proactive environmental policies that combat climate change, curb pollution, invest in renewable energy, and promote sustainable development solutions.

positions.summary: Filed an amicus brief with House Democrats urging the Supreme Court to overturn a Fifth Circuit decision restricting access to the abortion drug mifepristone.
positions.quote: Women deserve healthcare, and abortion care is healthcare. This lower court decision cannot stand.

positions.summary: Cosponsor of the Block the Bombs Act, which would end the shipment of weapons to Israel.
positions.quote: I have co-sponsored the Block the Bombs Act to end the shipment of destructive weapons to Israel.

positions.summary: Voted against a DHS funding bill that increased ICE's budget, saying there should be no additional ICE funding without reform of its tactics.
positions.quote: there should be no additional funding for ICE without meaningful reform

positions.summary: Member of the Congressional Safe Climate Caucus; says she is pushing for policies that combat climate change and invest in renewable energy instead of fossil fuels.
Describes herself as a staunch supporter of the Affordable Care Act and says she has fought to close the Medicaid coverage gap for North Carolinians.
Says her fiscal approach means tax increases for the wealthy and tax cuts for the middle class.
positions.quote: This means tax increases for the wealthy and tax cuts for the middle class.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Agriculture and the Committee on Education and the Workforce for the 2025-2026 Congress.

candidates.name: Jack Codiga
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 67.4% of the vote.

summary.text: Jack Codiga is the Republican nominee for North Carolina's 12th Congressional District. A California native who moved to Charlotte in 2021, he works in finance as an associate producer at the mortgage lender Medalist Capital and has not previously held elected office. His campaign website calls for abolishing the Federal Reserve and returning to gold- and silver-backed money.

background.text: Graduated from Scotts Valley High School and earned a bachelor's degree in finance from Santa Clara University's Leavey School of Business.
Moved to Charlotte from California in 2021, according to WFAE's 2026 voter guide.
Works in finance; WFAE lists his occupation as associate producer at Medalist Capital, a mortgage lender. He describes himself as "a Christian, finance professional, and proud American."
Has no previous experience in elected office, according to WFAE; won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary over Addul Ali with 67.4% of the vote.

priorities.text: Supports abolishing the Federal Reserve and returning currency control to the U.S. Treasury backed by gold and silver, which he says would address the rising cost of housing and other basics.
priorities.quote: I support ending the Federal Reserve, which currently controls our money and oversees a banking system where new money is created through loans. Control of our currency should return to the U.S. Treasury, with gold and silver once again serving as money.

priorities.text: Supports opening up primary elections so more candidates can compete, through a majority-winner or top-two runoff system.
priorities.quote: One of my priorities is giving voters more real choices by opening up the primary system so more candidates can compete. This would require either a majority winner or a runoff between the top two candidates, encouraging voters to choose based on principles instead of party labels.

priorities.text: Says immigration is his most passionate policy area and supports deporting violent criminals and those who abuse government programs.
priorities.quote: We need a clear approach that starts with deporting violent criminals and those who abuse government programs.

positions.summary: Supports a federal abortion ban, saying life begins at conception.
positions.quote: I support a federal abortion ban because I believe life begins at conception and that the right to life should be protected equally across state lines.

positions.summary: Supports deporting violent criminals and those abusing government programs, and removing welfare incentives for unlawful residency, while supporting a path to lawful residency for some who arrived as children.
positions.quote: We need a clear approach that starts with deporting violent criminals and those who abuse government programs. For others, we should remove incentives, like welfare benefits, that encourage illegal residency.

positions.summary: Supports constitutional carry and opposes legal hurdles to carrying a firearm.
positions.quote: States should not create burdensome legal hurdles just to carry a firearm.

positions.summary: Supports zoning reform limited to genuine infrastructure or pollution concerns, and opposes tax incentives that treat homes as investments rather than shelter.
positions.quote: Sound money would address much of this, but tax and zoning reform are also essential... Zoning should be limited to genuine infrastructure or pollution concerns.

positions.summary: Criticizes the influence of the Israel lobby (AIPAC) on U.S. politics as part of a broader call to register and restrict foreign agents' political influence.
positions.quote: A clear gap in the system is AIPAC, the Israel lobby, which has too much influence in our politics.

positions.summary: Supports ending government-backed health programs, including Social Security and government healthcare, in favor of a free-market approach.
positions.quote: End all welfare programs, including the godfather of all Ponzi schemes (Social Security), government healthcare, and government-backed mortgages. These programs create dependency, increase costs, and suppress wealth creation.

positions.summary: Supports abolishing the 16th Amendment (federal income tax) and property taxes in favor of user-based taxes and tariffs.
positions.quote: Property taxes should be illegal, and the 16th Amendment (income tax) should be abolished. America should rely on simpler, user-based taxes and tariffs.
